title: What Does the Bible Say About Gluttony? 26 Verses
description: Is gluttony a sin? What Proverbs, Paul and Jesus say about overeating, self-control and the body, with 26 verses.
keywords: what does the bible say about gluttony
bible verses about self-control and eating
summary: The Bible condemns gluttony in plain terms, though the word is rare: forms of glutton appear in only 6 verses of the World English Bible and 4 of the King James Version. Proverbs 23:20-21 warns against joining those who gorge on meat because the glutton comes to poverty, and Paul describes people whose god is their belly (Philippians 3:19). Jesus was accused of being a glutton and a drunkard for eating with sinners (Matthew 11:19), which shows the label could be a smear. Scripture treats food as a good gift (1 Timothy 4:4, Ecclesiastes 5:18) and puts the problem in a lack of self-control, which Paul lists as fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:23). The verses below cover the warnings, the gift and the discipline.

faqs.a: Yes, the Bible treats habitual overindulgence as sin. Proverbs 23:20-21 and 28:7 warn against gluttons, Deuteronomy 21:20 pairs glutton with drunkard, and Paul says those whose god is their belly are headed for destruction (Philippians 3:18-19). Christian tradition later listed gluttony among the seven deadly sins. The Bible's emphasis is on being mastered by appetite, not on how much any one meal weighs (1 Corinthians 6:12).

faqs.q: How many times is gluttony mentioned in the Bible?
faqs.a: Forms of the word glutton appear in 6 verses of the World English Bible (Deuteronomy 21:20, Proverbs 23:21, 28:7, Matthew 11:19, Luke 7:34, Titus 1:12) and 4 verses of the King James Version, which uses winebibber in the Gospels. Related passages on excess, self-control and appetite are far more numerous.

Yes. Jesus says people called him a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners (Matthew 11:19, Luke 7:34). He was contrasted with John the Baptist, who fasted. The charge was false, and it shows that opponents used the word as an insult for anyone who enjoyed a meal with the wrong company.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about overeating and health?
faqs.a: Paul says the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit and tells believers to glorify God in it (1 Corinthians 6:19-20), and to do everything, even eating and drinking, to the glory of God (1 Corinthians 10:31). Proverbs 25:16 says to eat only as much as you need, lest you vomit. None of these verses set a diet, and they frame eating as an act of self-control and gratitude.
